summary: Security audit of Task 1 (backend data layer + SignedDownloadToken HMAC-SHA256 crypto primitive, commit 9acd6e9). The signed-download-token primitive is correct and robust against the targeted OWASP/crypto concerns: HMAC-SHA256 is computed over the EXACT base64url payload segment (not decoded JSON), defeating JSON-whitespace/re-emission forgery; comparison uses MessageDigest.isEqual (constant-time, length-safe); the signature is verified BEFORE JSON parsing and expiry is checked only after the signature is trusted, so tampered payloads can neither reach the Jackson parser nor flip the failure reason to EXPIRED; cross-project substitution is rejected because projectId is bound inside the signed payload (verify returns the parsed projectId for the endpoint to match against the URL path); tamper/substitution/expiry/malformed cases all degrade to typed failures with no exception leakage. Key validation is fail-fast on blank/non-hex/wrong-length, the JDK HexFormat parse detail is scrubbed from the IllegalStateException message (offending char/index only recoverable at DEBUG via the attached cause), and the env-var name is surfaced — matching the TokenEncryptor precedent. No hardcoded secrets: .env.example carries only an empty placeholder, .env/.env.* are gitignored, and the zero-hex application.properties default is the spec-sanctioned test-friendly value that trips fail-fast on real deploys (mirrors app.bot.token-encryption-key). Jackson deserialization (A08) is safe: plain ObjectMapper, no polymorphic typing, fixed record with String/long fields, and it only runs on signature-verified bytes. No randomness is used in the token (deterministic HMAC by design — appropriate). New Mongo entities/indexes introduce no injection surface (static annotation-defined index defs, no string-concatenated queries; repository methods are derived/typed). No findings.
